Description
We are seeking a motivated PhD student interested in freshwater ecosystem ecology and biogeochemistry to join the Helton and Lawrence lab groups at the University of Connecticut beginning in January or June 2027. The student would be part of a broader interdisciplinary team investigating how beaver-created ecosystems in the Northeastern United States affect freshwater carbon cycling. The successful candidate would join the team as a Graduate Assistant (~$38,000 / year) and conduct field work to quantify greenhouse gas dynamics, ecosystem metabolism, and carbon stocks in ponds, wetlands, and streams. The student would also have the opportunity to develop approaches to model beaver-created ecosystem carbon dynamics at the watershed-scale.    

Required qualifications include an undergraduate degree in a related field and at least one year of post-baccalaureate research experience; fieldwork experience; interest and experience in biogeochemistry; and, excellent oral and written communication skills.  Two or more years of post-baccalaureate research experience or an MS degree in a related field is strongly preferred.   

We are committed to creating an inclusive and equitable working environment and encourage students from all backgrounds to apply. Interested? Please email Ashley Helton (Ashley.Helton@uconn.edu) by September 1, 2026 with the subject line “PhD Application Beaver Project”: 1) a statement of your research interests, and 2) a CV that includes relevant professional experience and contact information for three references. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Description
Ph.D. Graduate Research Assistantship
Florida Key Deer Ecology

Position Overview
The Texas A&M Natural Resources Institute (NRI) is seeking a highly motivated and qualified doctoral student for a project focused on Florida Key deer (Odocoileus virginianus clavium) ecology through the Department of Rangeland, Wildlife and Fisheries Management (RWFM) at Texas A&M University. This is a unique opportunity to conduct applied conservation research on an endangered subspecies of white-tailed deer located in a region with changing landscape characteristics ranging from urban development to climate change impacts.
 Project Description
The successful candidate will lead field-based research program investigating Key deer population abundance, distribution, and habitat use across the Lower Florida Keys. Proposed research project supports flexibility in defining research questions in collaboration with federal agency partners and may include broader species assessments (e.g., endangered Lower Keys marsh rabbit [Sylvilagus palustris hefneri] research). Research findings will contribute directly to the management and conservation of these federally listed threatened subspecies and inform recovery efforts coordinated with state and federal partners.
 Position Details
Appointment: Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA)
Duration: 3 years
Location: Field work conducted in the Lower Florida Keys, Florida, with academic affiliation through Texas A&M University
Salary: $32,000 that includes a tuition/fees stipend
Housing: Provided during field assignment
Minimum Qualifications
Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Ecology, or a closely related field required at time of appointment
Experience with field-oriented wildlife research
Strong quantitative and analytical skills
Experience with wildlife surveys and monitoring techniques
Proficiency in statistical software (e.g., R, Program MARK, or similar)
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in remote field conditions
Valid driver's license and clean driving record
Available to start as early as Fall 2026
 Preferred Qualifications
Experience with ungulate ecology and/or population modeling
Familiarity with distance sampling, occupancy modeling, or mark-recapture methods
Prior work in subtropical or island ecosystems
Strong publication record or demonstrated writing ability
Experience working with state or federal wildlife agencies
Responsibilities
Design and implement field data collection protocols for population abundance and distribution assessments
Collect, manage, and analyze ecological datasets
Collaborate with agency partners including the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and U.S. Navy in defining project scope
Publish research findings in peer-reviewed scientific journals
Present research at professional conferences
Contribute to program reports and outreach materials
Compensation and Benefits
Competitive graduate research assistantship stipend, may include teaching assistantship when in College Station.
Tuition waiver (per university policy)
Health insurance benefits
On-site housing potentially available
How to Apply
Interested applicants should submit the following materials as a single PDF to Drs. Roel Lopez (roel.lopez@ag.tamu.edu) and Israel Parker (israel.parker@ag.tamu.edu):
Cover letter describing your qualifications, research interests, and career goals (1 page maximum)
Curriculum vitae (CV)
Contact information for three professional references
Representative writing sample (thesis chapter or publication)
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.
About Texas A&M Natural Resources Institute
The Texas A&M Natural Resources Institute conducts applied research, technical assistance, and education programs to support the sustainable management of fish, wildlife, and natural resources. NRI works in close partnership with landowners, agencies, and conservation organizations across the nation. For more information, visit: nri.tamu.edu
Texas A&M University is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, age, or protected veteran status.

Israel Parker
israel.parker@ag.tamu.edu (preferred contact method)

ARS Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), National Cold Water Marine Aquaculture Center, located in Franklin, Maine

The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.

Research Project: Atlantic salmon are cultured all over the world to provide food for an ever-increasing population. To increase salmon production while maintaining product quality new ingredients must be found.  Protein and lipid ingredients make up most of the salmon feed. Determining the protein and lipid content, and fatty acid and amino acid profiles of potential ingredients is an important component for evaluation. This experience will enable you to learn about Atlantic salmon nutrition and fillet quality. Additionally, you may have the opportunity to go to an ARS experimental feed production facility to participate in making salmon diets for a study and visit other collaborators involved with this project. You will learn about salmon culture (salmon care) and experimental design while participating in this project.

Learning Objectives: 

Gain experience evaluating potential feed ingredients by determining protein and lipid content, as well as fatty acid and amino acid profiles.
Develop skills in nutritional analysis methods, including sample preparation, proximate analysis (crude lipid, crude fat, energy, ash, moisture), and astaxanthin analysis.
Learn how to perform fatty acid, amino acid, and particle size analyses to assess ingredient quality and suitability for salmon diets.
Understand how analytical results inform the formulation of efficient, high-quality diets for Atlantic salmon production.
Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Gary Burr (gary.burr@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.

Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.

Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process, please email ORISE.ARS.Northeast@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.

Description
1. Lower Wisconsin River Trap-and-Transfer Project
Description: During 2025 and 2026, in collaboration with Alliant Energy and the Wisconsin DNR we captured and transferred 50 blue suckers, 50 shovelnose sturgeon, and 20 lake sturgeon above Prairie Du Sac Dam on the Lower Wisconsin River to determine their behavior after transfer. Each fish was implanted with an acoustic transmitter. The student will largely be responsible for analysis of telemetry data using capture-recapture models with some field work associated with active tracking and downloading of acoustic receivers. 
 Qualifications: BS in Fisheries, Biology, Ecology or related field with GPA ≥ 3.0. Familiarity with acoustic telemetry data and using R preferred as this is largely an analytical exercise. However, some experience launching and navigating boats would be beneficial. 
 2. Green Bay Walleye Project: 
Description: During 2025, in collaboration with the Wisconsin and Michigan Departments of Natural Resources, acoustic transmitters were implanted into 140 walleye in northern Green Bay and 50 walleye from the Sturgeon Bay area to determine spawning locations. This project will involve extensive field work in 2027 and 2028 to download receivers and determine where eggs are deposited in the Sturgeon Bay area and whether larvae hatch at these locations. The project will also require analysis of a large telemetry data set.   
 Qualifications: BS in Fisheries, Biology, Ecology or related field with GPA ≥ 3.0. Extensive experience launching and navigating boats in a large lake environment is preferred. Some familiarity with the R programming language also preferred. Experience with acoustic telemetry technology and data would be beneficial. 
 3. Shovelnose Sturgeon Mortality Project: 
Description: We will use population information, Floy tag recovery information, and acoustic telemetry data collected by the Missouri Department of Conservation (MDC) for shovelnose sturgeon in the Mississippi and Missouri rivers to estimate and compare mortality rates for different river segments. This project is largely an analytical exercise that will focus on using length-based and capture-recapture models. 
 Qualifications: Familiarity with the R programming language preferred. Experience with acoustic telemetry technology and data would also be beneficial.

Description
Summary:

The incursion of a novel strain of highly pathogenic avian influenza into the United States since the winter of 2021/2022 has had large scale consequences for the health and populations of many wild bird species. While numerous species have been found to mount antibody responses after exposure to this viral threat, little is known about the sub-clinical
impacts of infection. This project will seek to analyze numerous immune health assays from plasma previously collected across a wide range of avian species of known avian influenza status and seek to identify differences in immune health assays as a function of current or previous AIV infection.
 Required expertise/skills:  
Experience with methods for analysis of plasma-based biomarkers of avian health is highly beneficial for this position, though specific assay techniques can be taught to the selected applicant. Experience with statistical analysis and data visualization is also desired. Experience with scientific writing is preferred.

Eligibility requirements:  To be eligible the candidate must have graduated (bachelor’s, masters, or Ph.D.) within the past 5 years, and should make their graduation date clear in application materials.

Compensation:  Approximately $52,000 annually

The ideal start date for the position is mid-August 2026 but earlier start dates are welcome and later start dates will be considered.  This is a 18 month position.
